title: Building an AI-assisted game made me realize how much a browser can actually do
author: Wide-Bobcat-3723
selftext:
One of the things that has genuinely blown me away while making Pelota is that you can plug in an Xbox or PlayStation controller and just play the same game in a browser tab. Now I have couch co-op with two controllers, and it feels so much better for this game than mouse and keyboard.

Pelota is a 3D Mesoamerican ballgame built with Three.js. You play against the Lords of Xibalba, striking the ball with your hips, knees and forearms. If you play FIFA / EA FC, a lot of the controller layout feels familiar, even though the sport itself is completely different.

Then there’s the online side. I’m using PeerJS for invite-only co-op: send a friend a link, they open it on their computer, and you’re on the same team. Getting multiplayer working has come with its own issues, but seeing this become something I can actually play with another person has been a huge part of the process.

I’m building it with heavy AI assistance: Claude for code, Meshy for characters and props, Mixamo for animations, and Suno for music. A lot of my work is deciding how it should feel, trying things, and figuring out what needs to change.

Another part of the journey has been reaching beyond the tools. I’ve been contacting subject-matter experts with questions about the ballgame and its history, and reaching out to Mexican streamers to get the game in front of people. One creator has already played it live, is preparing a more formal review, and has asked about interviewing me.

Those expert conversations are research, not historical approval of the game. I’m still learning, and there are details I want to get right rather than just accepting whatever an AI gives me.

The current alpha has a story opening with an injured older brother teaching you, a village, controller support, local and online co-op, and English and Spanish throughout.

It’s free to try at [https://pelota.io](https://pelota.io). I recommend a controller if you have one.
